why: Every change in who is on call happens at some rotation's start or end. Sweep those times in order, apply all +1/-1 events at each time, and emit the segment between consecutive event times when someone is on call; merge with the previous segment if the set did not actually change.
hints: Between two consecutive start/end times the on-call set cannot change. Which times matter?
Make events (time, name, +1) and (time, name, -1), group by time, and sweep. The segment [t_prev, t) carries the set that was active after processing t_prev.
Keep a count per name (the same person may overlap themselves) and a flag for whether membership changed at t_prev; skip empty segments. O(n log n) plus output size.
pitfalls: Half-open intervals: an end at 40 and a start at 40 meet with no gap and no overlap.
If one person's rotation ends exactly when their next one starts, the set does not change, so the segment must not be split.
Omit periods where no one is on call.
Sort names inside each output segment.
